title: Jet crashes on a Palm Beach County road, killing all nine aboard
caption: A Learjet flying from Austin to the Bahamas crashed nose-first onto Military Trail in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Nov. 1, killing all nine people aboard. It left a burning crater feet from homes; no one on the ground was reported hurt, and about 600 nearby mobile home residents were evacuated. The crew had reported icing and turbulence before a steep dive. The NTSB is investigating; no cause has been determined.

stories.name: Jet crashes on a Palm Beach County road, killing all nine aboard
facts: A Learjet 60 bound from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed around 12:50 p.m. on Nov. 1 near a residential area of Palm Beach County, Florida, coming down nose-first on Military Trail and leaving a burning crater in the road.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said all nine people aboard were killed; their identities had not been released. Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone hurt on the ground.
Witnesses told AP the jet landed feet from homes and close to passing vehicles. Thick black smoke covered the site; the road was closed in both directions.
Authorities evacuated about 600 residents of a nearby mobile home community. Rain was falling and a flood watch was in effect.
The NTSB is investigating with FAA support. Air traffic audio shows the crew reported icing and turbulence and asked to climb before a steep dive and a mayday; no cause has been determined.

artwork.alt: Graphic poster illustration on a rainy afternoon, looking down a wide suburban Florida road. A burning crater in the pavement sends a tall black smoke column up into storm clouds, with chunks of pavement around it. Low houses, palm trees and a mobile home park stand close on both sides, untouched. Firefighters spray water from a red fire engine; a deputy beside a striped barricade and a patrol car close the road; residents walk away under umbrellas. No aircraft or victims are shown.
